narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Conditions today felt much like yesterday — similar warmth, calmer winds, and dry again. Little has changed since earlier today, though high convective instability persists tonight peaking around 20:00, where models diverge sharply with UKMO building CAPE to 3780 J/kg while GFS shows minimal activity near 150 J/kg.

## Today's Forecast
With evening underway, daytime highs near 32°C / 90°F and solar UV exposure are in the past. For the remainder of tonight through midnight, skies will remain partly cloudy to overcast with temperatures dropping slowly through 24°C / 75°F toward an overnight low near 18°C / 64°F. Winds will stay light to gentle from the SW at 8–12 km/h (4–6 kt). Despite high atmospheric instability over the basin, dry mid-level air will keep surface precipitation at 0.0 mm (0.0 in). For Thursday morning, expect sunny intervals with temperatures climbing back toward 33°C / 91°F by early afternoon under south-westerly breezes. Ground air quality monitoring sensors are currently stale; model guidance indicates Moderate conditions near 76–77 US AQI overnight.

## Extended Outlook
Days 1 to 3 (Thursday through Saturday) will bring warm and dry conditions across Nyanza Basin, with daytime highs of 33°C to 34°C (91°F to 93°F) and overnight lows near 18°C / 64°F. Winds will remain light to moderate from the SW. Days 4 to 7 (Sunday through Wednesday) maintain dry conditions with high temperatures holding between 32°C and 33°C (90°F to 91°F). Rain probability remains low until early September, when ECMWF and ICON indicate a slight chance of isolated showers (0.2–2.5 mm / 0.01–0.10 in).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe surface rainfall or flash flooding hazards are anticipated tonight or tomorrow. Elevated convective instability (CAPE > 3000 J/kg on UKMO) tonight creates a localized potential for isolated thunder and lightning over Lake Victoria, even though surface rainfall totals will remain at 0.0 mm (0.0 in). Midday UV exposure tomorrow will again reach Very High levels (8.8–9.1).

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
For tonight, boaters on open lake waters can expect south-westerly winds averaging 11–18 km/h (6–10 kt) with gusts up to 28 km/h (15 kt), relaxing toward dawn. Lake surface temperatures remain near 18°C / 64°F with light chop. On Thursday, morning easterly breezes will back to the SW by afternoon, increasing to 15–23 km/h (8–12 kt) with gusts reaching 33 km/h (18 kt). Boaters should remain aware of potential evening electrical activity over open waters given elevated atmospheric instability across the lake basin.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1006 hPa) and highest toward the south (1019 hPa) — a 13 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the north, while pressure overhead is near-steady. Local land-lake breezes remain the dominant driver for diurnal surface wind shifts.

Ground air quality monitoring stations (Kisumu Airport at 57 US AQI, Ochieng' Avenue at 61 US AQI, and Dunga Beach at 53 US AQI) have not updated in over 3 hours (3.4 hours old) and are considered stale. Operational assessment relies on CAMS model guidance showing Moderate air quality (PM2.5 driven, 76–78 US AQI).

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Little has changed in the guidance since this morning's forecast update. ECMWF and ICON maintain strong Day+0 rain verification skill (70% rolling accuracy) compared to GFS (40% rolling accuracy) and UKMO (declining trend at 30% rolling accuracy). The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecast for Kisumu calls for sunny intervals with daytime highs of 31°C / 88°F and lows of 18°C / 64°F for tomorrow (August 27), agreeing with the multi-model numerical consensus. For the extended range (Day+3 and Day+7), ECMWF and Best Match hold the strongest track records, though Day+7 evaluations remain limited to 8 historical checks.

morning_issuance.narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Conditions today will feel much like yesterday — similar warmth, calmer winds, and dry again, with maximum temperatures reaching around 32°C / 90°F under partly cloudy skies.

## Today's Forecast
This morning brings clear to partly cloudy conditions with mild temperatures near 18°C / 64°F and light northeasterly winds. Through midday, temperatures will climb rapidly to a high of 32°C / 90°F, accompanied by a wind shift to the southwest at 12–17 km/h (6–9 kt). Peak UV index will reach 9.1 (Very High) around noon; sun protection is recommended between 10:00 and 15:00. During the late afternoon and evening, convective energy (CAPE) builds significantly across the region (peaking between 1100 and 2600 J/kg across models), which may trigger cloud development and elevated lightning overhead or over the lake, but surface precipitation is expected to remain at 0.0 mm (0.0 in). Overnight temperatures will drop to 18°C / 64°F under variable cloud cover. Air quality will sit in the Moderate range (US AQI ~78, primary driver PM2.5).

## Extended Outlook
Days 1 to 3 (Thursday through Saturday) promise continued warm and sunny weather with daytime highs ranging from 33°C to 34°C (91°F to 93°F) and overnight lows near 18°C / 64°F. Winds will stay moderate from the south-southwest. Days 4 to 7 (Sunday through Wednesday) maintain dry conditions with high temperatures gently cooling toward 32°C / 90°F. Rain probability stays below 15% until Wednesday, when ECMWF introduces a minor shower risk (0.2 mm / 0.01 in).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe rainfall or flooding hazards are expected today. High convective instability (CAPE > 2000 J/kg on UKMO and ICON) during late afternoon and evening could generate localized thunder and lightning over Lake Victoria and neighboring ridges, but rainfall totals will stay near 0.0 mm (0.0 in). Midday UV exposure (9.1 max) presents the main daily health hazard.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Boaters across open waters can expect morning winds from the east-southeast at 15–22 km/h (8–12 kt). Winds will back to the south-southwest by mid-afternoon, increasing to 18–26 km/h (10–14 kt) with gusts up to 36 km/h (19 kt). Lake surface waters remain around 18°C / 64°F. Light chop in the morning will transition to moderate chop by late afternoon. Boaters should remain aware of potential late-day electrical activity over the water despite dry surface conditions.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1006 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1019 hPa) — a 12 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Locally across Nyanza Basin, mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.8 hPa in Kisumu and 1015.0 hPa in the southern highlands, dropping by about 1.5 hPa over the next 24 hours. Diurnal land-lake breeze thermal circulation will drive localized wind shifts from E/NE in the morning to SW/W in the afternoon. Deep atmospheric moisture remains insufficient for widespread convective cloud tops, capping precipitable water despite substantial evening convective energy (CAPE > 2000 J/kg).

Ground air quality monitoring stations currently report: Kisumu Airport (63 US AQI), Ochieng' Avenue (54 US AQI), and Dunga Beach (49 US AQI). However, all ground sensor readings are currently stale (3 hours old), so operational air quality assessment relies on CAMS reanalysis model data showing Moderate conditions (~77-81 US AQI).

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
At Day+0, recent verification track records heavily favor ICON (90% rolling 10-check rain accuracy) and ECMWF (70% accuracy) over GFS (declining to 20%). GFS continues to show a systematic wind speed over-prediction bias (+18.7 km/h error yesterday). For the extended forecast (Day+3 and Day+7), ECMWF and Best Match show stronger track records (60-70% rain verification). Note that at Day+7, only 8 checks are recorded for GFS and ECMWF, which is directional only and does not yet support ranking models against one another.
